title: A neural command circuit for grooming movement control
source_locator: Fig. 2A,B; Results 'Three different interneuron classes elicit antennal grooming'
quote: experiments to thermogenetically activate aDN1 or aDN2 alone indicate that they are each sufficient to induce antennal grooming
mapping_basis: synonyms.csv/type_list.csv list aDN1 (Hampel 2015) as a literature name of DNg62 only; driver_lines.csv also maps aDN1-spGAL4-1 to DNg62.
stimulation: 30-31 C, 2 min video recording (lines screened at 30-32 C)
penetrance: aDN1-spGAL4-1 flies spent 4.8% of time antennal grooming (vs 66.1% for aBN2-spGAL4-2)
n_flies_note: Fig. 2 legend: n >= 9 flies per spGAL4
notes: Antennal grooming is done by the front legs (paper: 'front leg movements necessary for antennal grooming'); middle/hind legs not described. Effect is weak (4.8% of time). Text implies split lines exclusive for aDN1/aDN2 but not verified, so specificity left unknown. Methods: '5-8 day old males were used for all experiments'.

title: A neural command circuit for grooming movement control
source_locator: Fig. 7C,D; Fig. 7-figure supplement 1A,B; Results 'A circuit whose components elicit different durations of antennal grooming'
quote: Indeed, activation of aDN1 or aDN2 caused grooming that did not outlast the red light activation
mapping_basis: aDN1 is a literature name of DNg62 only (synonyms.csv); aDN1-spGAL4-1 -> DNg62 in driver_lines.csv.
stimulation: 656 nm red light, 27 mW/cm2, 5 Hz (0.1 s on/off) for 5 s, 30 s interstimulus interval, 3 stimulations

n_flies_note: Fig. 7-fig supp 1 legend: 10-15 flies shown for each spGAL4 pair

title: A neural command circuit for grooming movement control

stimulation: 656 nm red light, 27 mW/cm2, 5 Hz (0.1 s on/off) for 5 s, 30 s interstimulus interval, 3 stimulations

n_flies_note: Fig. 7-fig supp 1 legend: 10-15 flies shown for each spGAL4 pair

title: Descending networks transform command signals into population motor control
source_locator: Fig. 1b, Fig. 2, Fig. 4c,g (intact); Extended Data Fig. 1d; Results
mapping_basis: aDN2 is a literature name of DNfl023 only (synonyms.csv); driver_lines.csv maps R76F12-AD;R18C11-DBD to DNfl023 from this paper's split-GAL4 table.
stimulation: 640 nm laser on neck connective, 41.6 uW, 5 s on / 10 s off
penetrance: flies groom only at highest power (41.6 uW); at 21 uW mostly stop/rest
n_flies_note: Fig. 2: n = 3 flies, 34 trials; Fig. 4 intact/headless panels: n = 5 flies, 10 trials each
notes: Text: 'groom upon aDN2 stimulation only for the highest stimulation power (41.6 uW) but rest at 21 uW'. Leg keypoints tracked with SLEAP (front leg approach); middle/hind legs not described for grooming. All experiments on female flies.

title: Descending networks transform command signals into population motor control
quote: aDN2 stimulation in both intact and headless animals leads to front leg approach
mapping_basis: aDN2 is a literature name of DNfl023 only (synonyms.csv); R76F12-AD;R18C11-DBD -> DNfl023 in driver_lines.csv.
stimulation: 640 nm laser on neck connective, 41.6 uW, 5 s on / 10 s off
penetrance: antennal grooming lost after decapitation (Fig. 4c, P = 0.006); front leg approach retained
n_flies_note: Fig. 4: n = 5 flies with 10 trials each
notes: Results: 'DNp09 and aDN2 stimulation in headless animals did not elicit forwards walking ... or antennal grooming (Fig. 4c; P = 0.006), respectively.' Front leg approach (tibia-tarsus to neck distance) coded as a single reaching movement (front = no); category 'other'. Middle/hind legs not described.
